claims.claim: The best-performing setup, OpenAI's o1-preview with AIDE scaffolding, achieves at least the level of a Kaggle bronze medal in 16.9% of competitions on MLE-bench.
claims.quote: finding that the best-performing setup--OpenAI's o1-preview with AIDE scaffolding--achieves at least the level of a Kaggle bronze medal in 16.9% of competitions

claims.claim: A Claude v3 Opus agent achieves a 37.5% average success rate across tasks in MLAgentBench.
claims.quote: We benchmark agents based on Claude v1.0, Claude v2.1, Claude v3 Opus, GPT-4, GPT-4-turbo, Gemini-Pro, and Mixtral and find that a Claude v3 Opus agent is the best in terms of success rate. It can build compelling ML models over many tasks in MLAgentBench with 37.5% average success rate.

claims.claim: Success rates on MLAgentBench vary from 100% on well-established older datasets to 0% on recent Kaggle challenges potentially created after the underlying LM was trained.
claims.quote: However, the success rates vary considerably; they span from 100% on well-established older datasets to as low as 0% on recent Kaggle challenges created potentially after the underlying LM was trained.

claims.claim: The best pairing of search strategy and operator set increases the success rate of achieving a Kaggle medal on MLE-bench lite from 39.6% to 47.7%.
claims.quote: Our best pairing of search strategy and operator set achieves a state-of-the-art result on MLE-bench lite, increasing the success rate of achieving a Kaggle medal from 39.6% to 47.7%.

claims.claim: MLE-STAR achieves medals in 64% of the Kaggle competitions on MLE-bench Lite.
claims.quote: Our experimental results show that MLE-STAR achieves medals in 64% of the Kaggle competitions on the MLE-bench Lite, significantly outperforming the best alternative.

open_questions: What are the success rates for other model-scaffold combinations on MLE-bench beyond o1-preview + AIDE?
How do success rates on MLE-bench lite compare to the full MLE-bench benchmark?
What are the success rates for agents on MLAgentBench using more recent models (post-2023) like GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, etc.?
How often do LLM-agent-written ML programs run without errors (as opposed to achieving medal-level performance)?
What are the failure modes and error rates for agents on these benchmarks?
